title: Optimizing LLM Queries in Relational Data Analytics Workloads
problem: LLM batch inference over relational tables is extremely slow and expensive because naive row-order invocation achieves low KV cache prefix hit rates, wasting prefill computation on repeated data patterns.
motivation: Relational data contains systematic repetition (foreign keys, joined metadata, repeated categories) that creates prefix-sharing opportunities across rows. A fixed default field ordering in SQL leaves much of this sharing unexploited. With full knowledge of the batch, optimal reordering can dramatically increase prefix cache hit rates.
method: The method reorders rows and fields to maximize KV cache prefix hits—reusing previously computed results when the same data patterns repeat. It uses two algorithms: OPHR (Optimal Prefix Hit Recursion) recursively splits the table by distinct field values for the mathematically optimal ordering but is exponentially slow, while GGR (Greedy Group Recursion) approximates this by greedily selecting the highest-impact field and value at each step. GGR further optimizes by using functional dependencies to group related fields and value statistics to skip unnecessary work, processing tables up to 30K rows with 57 fields in under 15 seconds via PySpark and vLLM.
key_novelty: The key contribution is using relational database structure—how fields depend on each other, and value distributions—to reorder rows and fields, so language models can reuse more previously computed results when processing data in batches.
contributions: Formal definition of Prefix Hit Count (PHC) objective for LLM query optimization
OPHR: provably optimal recursive reordering algorithm
GGR: efficient greedy approximation leveraging functional dependencies and table statistics
Proof that per-row field reordering beats fixed field ordering by up to m times in PHC
16-query benchmark across 7 real-world datasets (Movies, Products, BIRD, PDMX, Beer, SQuAD, FEVER)
32% cost savings with OpenAI/Anthropic prompt caching pricing

metrics.speedup: 1.5-3.4x end-to-end query latency speedup vs Cache (Original); 1.8-3.8x vs No Cache
metrics.accuracy: Within 5% accuracy of original ordering (except FEVER+Llama3-8B where GGR is +14.2% better)
metrics.other: 32% cost savings on OpenAI GPT-4o-mini; up to 79% estimated savings with Anthropic auto-prefix caching; GGR runs in <15s for 30K rows x 57 fields

limitations: Assumes offline batch mode with full table visibility; not applicable to streaming queries
PHC objective assumes exact-match prefix sharing; substring matches not exploited
OPHR is exponential complexity, impractical for large tables; GGR is an approximation
